changes_vs_current: New topic. Raw average-position order (9 scored people sources, missing = 29): Dog, Cat, Bird, Rabbit, Fish, Horse, Snake, Lizard, Turtle, Ferret, Hamster, Guinea Pig, Chicken, Pig, Goat, Tarantula, Axolotl, Mouse, Rat, Gerbil, Duck, Hedgehog, Hermit Crab (Frog unscored, qualitative only). All 12 gut-check answers were already in the raw top 12. Moves: Fish 5 -> 3 (third in every source that measures it: APPA, Harris, Gallup, AVMA, SurveyMonkey; its raw spot only reflects absence from the dating/backyard/search lists, which did not ask about fish). Hamster 11 -> 6 (5th in Gallup with guinea pigs and 5th in SurveyMonkey; tied with reptiles and horses in Gallup at 2%; gut check; its raw spot comes from not being asked about in APPA/Harris categories, which lump it into small animal/rodent). Horse 6 -> 7, Turtle 9 -> 8 (ahead of snake and lizard in AVMA household counts, 1,320k vs 555k/725k), Snake 7 -> 9, Lizard 8 -> 10, Guinea Pig 12 -> 11 above Ferret (AVMA 847k vs 334k households; ferret is lifted by search interest and Harris 4%). Hermit Crab moved above Hedgehog and Duck (single-source tie; hermit crabs are a very common kids' pet). Frog placed #24 on AVMA naming amphibians among rising specialty pets (no figure). Granularity: parrots/parakeets/budgies folded into Bird; goldfish/betta into Fish; geckos/bearded dragons/iguanas into Lizard; tortoise into Turtle; rooster/hen into Chicken; spider into Tarantula, so no two items share an animal. Left out for lack of data: chinchilla, sugar glider, cow.
confidence: medium. Dog, Cat, Fish, Bird are solid across every ownership source (APPA 2025, Harris 2024, Gallup, AVMA). Positions 5-12 (rabbit, hamster, horse, reptiles, guinea pig, ferret) are all well supported as the next tier but their exact order shifts between sources and several sources only report lumped categories (small animal, reptile, rodent). The tail (13-24) leans on one or two sources each (AVMA 2012 specialty table, USDA backyard study, SurveyMonkey mentions, 2021 search data); Frog at #24 has only qualitative AVMA support, and no source found for chinchilla.
